posts.title: Why Do We Procrastinate Even When We know Better?
posts.subheadline: You are aware that the deadline is nearing and that the work must be completed. Suddenly, checking your phone, watching a video or doing something completely different becomes much easier. Why is it that we love to put things off?
posts.cardSummary: Procrastination is frequently viewed as laziness, but there is more to the psychology of procrastination. It is defined by researchers as needlessly postponing ...
posts.bodyContent:
Procrastination is frequently viewed as laziness, but there is more to the psychology of procrastination. It is defined by researchers as needlessly postponing a desired action when there is a potential for harm. Research is becoming more and more associated with the link between procrastination and emotion regulation. Sometimes, we don't want to do something because we don't want the feeling we get from the result rather than the action itself.

Think of arriving at an assignment and being overwhelmed by it. You don't start, instead you look at social media. This is a short-term discomfort that lasts for a few minutes. That temporary relief can reinforce the habit, making it easier to repeat the behaviour later.

Even clues could be found within the brain. An MRI study published in Psychological Science in 2018 identified the amygdala as a brain area that is associated with procrastination. The people with less action control had a larger amygdala and weaker links between the amygdala and the dorsal anterior cingulate cortex, which is part of the brain that controls actions.

But that doesn't mean that a bigger amygdala leads to procrastination. The study found an association, but not a direct cause, and more research is required to understand the mechanisms in the brain, researchers said.

posts.title: Alejandro Betancourt: The Controversial Oilman at the Center of Trump’s Venezuela Strategy
posts.subheadline: A businessman investigated for alleged corruption and money laundering has become a key intermediary between Washington and Delcy Rodríguez, raising questions about who is really benefiting from Venezuela’s oil reopening
posts.cardSummary: Venezuela's oil industry is undergoing one of the most dramatic transformations in decades. Under the Trump administration, Washington is pushing to reopen the ...
posts.bodyContent:
Venezuela's oil industry is undergoing one of the most dramatic transformations in decades. Under the Trump administration, Washington is pushing to reopen the country's enormous energy sector to American investment. But at the center of this process is a controversial Venezuelan businessman: Alejandro Betancourt.

Betancourt has become an important intermediary between the Trump administration and the government of Delcy Rodríguez. Former Trump adviser Mauricio Claver-Carone acknowledged that U.S. officials used Betancourt because he understood both the Venezuelan and American oil industries and could connect the two sides. The controversy comes from Betancourt's past.

He became wealthy during the Chávez era through Derwick Associates, a company that obtained billions of dollars in Venezuelan energy contracts. Transparency International previously estimated that Derwick's contracts involved approximately $2.9 billion in alleged overbilling, allegations that Betancourt and the company have denied.

More seriously, Betancourt is currently under investigation in Spain and Switzerland over alleged money laundering, tax fraud and corruption connected to Venezuelan oil operations. Spanish authorities reopened a case in June involving allegations that $42 million in bribes were paid to Venezuelan state-oil officials as part of a scheme involving billions of dollars in currency transactions. Betancourt denies wrongdoing and has never been convicted of a crime. Yet despite these investigations, his influence over Venezuela's oil sector has increased.

posts.title: Venezuela’s Transition Is Moving. But Too Slowly to Solve the Country’s Immediate Problems
posts.subheadline: Judicial reforms, political prisoner releases and economic reopening show real progress, but millions of Venezuelans are still waiting for concrete improvements in their daily lives
posts.cardSummary: Venezuela's post-Maduro transition has produced several important developments in 2026, but the process remains considerably slower than the urgency of the coun...
posts.bodyContent:
Venezuela's post-Maduro transition has produced several important developments in 2026, but the process remains considerably slower than the urgency of the country's problems demands.

The first major achievement has been the opening of formal negotiations between the government of interim President Delcy Rodríguez and part of the opposition. The first round concluded in August with an agreement to begin transforming the judicial system, including the replacement of the Supreme Tribunal's magistrates through a new selection process. The sides also agreed to seek access to Venezuelan reserves frozen in the Bank of England to help finance earthquake reconstruction.

These are significant steps. Venezuela's judiciary has long been criticized for its dependence on the executive, and the Supreme Tribunal validated Nicolás Maduro's disputed 2024 electoral victory. Reforming that institution could therefore become one of the foundations of a future democratic system.

There has also been movement on political prisoners. An amnesty law approved in February facilitated the release of hundreds of detainees, while Rodríguez announced another 131 releases in August. Yet human-rights organizations reported that hundreds remained imprisoned, and many released individuals continued to face restrictions.

posts.title: Why Do Hot Springs Really Get Hot? The Solution Begins Far Below Your Feet
posts.subheadline: There is absolutely no heat at the beginning of the bubbling water. On a long, deep detour, it is rainfall.
posts.cardSummary: With no stove or fire in sight, the water rising directly out of the ground and already steaming appears almost miraculous. The true explanation begins far earl...
posts.bodyContent:
With no stove or fire in sight, the water rising directly out of the ground and already steaming appears almost miraculous. The true explanation begins far earlier than most people realize and much below the surface. Before it ever reappears as something you would like to swim in, the majority of hot springs start out as perfectly normal rain or groundwater that seeps through fissures and faults in the Earth's crust, often for years.

What, then, heats it during the process? Depending on the location, there are two primary routes. Groundwater can come into direct touch with shallow pockets of magma, or molten rock that is relatively close to the surface, in areas where volcanism is active. This causes the water to heat up significantly as it goes by. In locations without volcanic activity, heat is generated by something slower and more consistent: the geothermal gradient, which is simply the fact that rock temperature rises as you go deeper beneath. When water seeps far enough, it finally comes into contact with rock that is hot enough to warm it without the need for magma.

The water does not stay down there either way. When heated, it loses density relative to the surrounding cooler water, which causes it to rise through fissures and cracks until it eventually emerges as a hot spring. A hot spring can become a geyser by periodically erupting if the underground plumbing system is precisely constructed to hold pressure until it bursts abruptly.

posts.title: Peter Cullen, the Legendary Voice of Optimus Prime and Eeyore, Dies at 85
posts.subheadline: The legendary Canadian voice actor gave life to Optimus Prime, Eeyore and dozens of other memorable characters across a career spanning more than five decades.
posts.cardSummary: For generations of fans, Optimus Prime had a voice. Now, that voice has fallen silent.Peter Cullen, the acclaimed Canadian voice actor best known for portraying...
posts.bodyContent:
For generations of fans, Optimus Prime had a voice. Now, that voice has fallen silent.

Peter Cullen, the acclaimed Canadian voice actor best known for portraying the heroic leader of the Autobots in Transformers, has died at the age of 85. Cullen died on August 26 at his home in Los Angeles, surrounded by his family, according to his agent and family. His cause of death has not been disclosed.

Cullen first became the voice of Optimus Prime in the original 1984 animated Transformers series, establishing the deep, authoritative voice that would become inseparable from the character. He later returned to the role across animated productions, video games and Michael Bay’s live-action Transformers films.

His portrayal of Optimus Prime was more than simply a distinctive voice. Cullen helped shape the character as a leader defined by strength, compassion and responsibility. He drew inspiration for the character's voice from his brother Larry, a Vietnam War veteran and former U.S. Marine.

But Optimus Prime was only one part of Cullen’s extraordinary career.

He was also widely recognized as Eeyore in Disney’s Winnie the Pooh productions, bringing his famously deep voice to the gloomy but beloved donkey. His other credits included KARR in Knight Rider, King Kong in the 1976 film and the vocal effects for the Predator in the 1987 science-fiction action movie.

posts.title: Jonathan Meléndez: A Brutal Crime That Has Shocked Mexico
posts.subheadline: The murder of the Camilo Séptimo musician, his pregnant wife, their young daughter and a domestic worker has reignited concerns about violence, criminality and insecurity in Mexico.
posts.cardSummary: Mexico's music community has been shaken by the murder of Jonathan Samuel Meléndez Ochoa, known professionally as “Honas,” a 38-year-old keyboardist, composer a...
posts.bodyContent:
Mexico's music community has been shaken by the murder of Jonathan Samuel Meléndez Ochoa, known professionally as “Honas,” a 38-year-old keyboardist, composer and producer and one of the founding members of the alternative band Camilo Séptimo. Meléndez was killed alongside his wife, their three-year-old daughter and a 21-year-old domestic worker inside the family's apartment in Atizapán de Zaragoza, State of Mexico.

The attack occurred on September 1 in the Grand Viure residential complex in the Bosque Esmeralda area. According to the State of Mexico prosecutor's office, the victims were found after neighbors reported screams and possible gunshots. Two of the victims had been restrained, while the victims suffered fatal gunshot wounds. The family's dog was also found dead.

Meléndez's wife, Ana Paola, was pregnant at the time of the attack. Their six-year-old son survived after hiding inside the apartment and was found physically unharmed. The brutality of the crime has generated particular outrage because the victims were apparently targeted inside their own home, in a residential area considered relatively secure.

Investigators have arrested two men in connection with the killings. One of them, Diego Sebastián “N,” was a business associate of Meléndez. Authorities are investigating whether financial disagreements connected to a property-rental business were behind the attack. However, the motive has not yet been definitively established, and the suspects remain legally presumed innocent. Mexican authorities continue investigating the circumstances surrounding the crime. The fact that one suspect allegedly knew Meléndez is particularly significant. Investigators believe that his relationship with the musician may have allowed him to enter the residence without immediately raising suspicion.

posts.title: British Couple Seriously Injured After Being Trapped in Deadly Spain Wildfires
posts.subheadline: A British couple were rescued from a ravine in Spain's Almería province after becoming trapped in the devastating wildfires that have swept across the region, according to local reports.
posts.cardSummary: The couple, believed to have been hiking when the fire spread rapidly through the area on Thursday, were discovered in critical condition by Civil Guard officer...
posts.bodyContent:
The couple, believed to have been hiking when the fire spread rapidly through the area on Thursday, were discovered in critical condition by Civil Guard officers conducting a search operation near the village of Bédar. Both suffered severe burns and were airlifted to hospital, where they remain in intensive care.

The wildfires have already claimed 12 lives, making them among the deadliest in Spain's recent history. Local authorities have reported that more than 6,600 hectares (16,300 acres) of land have been destroyed. While the identities of those who died have not yet been officially confirmed, reports suggest that four of the victims may have been British nationals.

Dramatic Rescue

The couple were found in the early hours of Friday after rescuers heard faint cries for help coming from a steep ravine.

"As you gain more experience, something inside you tells you, 'Look again, try one more time,'" Civil Guard Sergeant Pedro Barre told Spanish broadcaster TVE.

Following the sound, officers climbed down the hillside and located the pair. Rescue officials said both victims were semi-conscious and had burns covering approximately 40% of their bodies.

"Being able to call out in the condition they were in was a titanic effort," said rescuer Rafael Zea.

Barre added: "We'll never forget the look of surprise and emotion on their faces."

Fire Situation Improving

Emergency services have continued containment and recovery operations across the affected region. On Sunday, Andalusian regional president Juan Manuel Moreno Bonilla announced that the wildfire had been contained and its perimeter secured, allowing authorities to lower the emergency alert level.

posts.title: US Sailors reach a Thai beach town after 250 Days at Sea and a War They Didn't Sign Up For.
posts.subheadline: The USS Abraham Lincoln departed from San Diego with six-months’ worth of mission time in the Pacific scheduled. Instead, it crashed in Iran and its 5,000-member crew has not come into contact with land for more than eight months.
posts.cardSummary: The nuclear-powered aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln has arrived off the coast of Thailand in Pattaya, about 250 days since it set sail without stopping a s...
posts.bodyContent:
The nuclear-powered aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln has arrived off the coast of Thailand in Pattaya, about 250 days since it set sail without stopping a single port—finally, a respite for the ship's crew of nearly 5,000 sailors and Marines. It was supposed to be a routine 6-month assignment across the Pacific and South China Sea for the carrier, which left San Diego last November.

So, what did keep it afloat for nearly 2000 years?

In war, and not that it was used for. The ship was diverted to the Gulf in the wake of US and Israeli military actions against Iran in late February, in which Admiral Cooper says the Lincoln dropped over 1.5 million pounds of weaponry and flew over 10,000 sorties. The situation on board allegedly deteriorated to the point where there were concerns to the Congress about food shortages, broken toilets and mental stress on the crew. The Navy acknowledged the deployment was difficult, but didn't elaborate on the Pattaya stop, citing "operational security".

posts.title: You May Be Getting More Out of Your Sugar-Free Gum Than Just Breath Freshness
posts.subheadline: A long-held belief that artificial sweeteners flow through the body without having any effect on your heart or metabolism is being challenged by new studies.
posts.cardSummary: Chewingum(PHOTO: GETTY IMAGES) Chewing gum and other sugar-free items were promoted for years as the guilt-free, safe alternative to sugar that was delicious wi...
posts.bodyContent:
Chewing gum and other sugar-free items were promoted for years as the guilt-free, safe alternative to sugar that was delicious without the negative effects on metabolism. According to two distinct investigations, the assumption is no longer valid.

The first followed 17,710 individuals over a 30-year period and was presented at the annual meeting of the European Society of Cardiology. Researchers from Berlin's Charité University Hospital found that those with the highest blood levels of xylitol had a 57% increased risk of heart attack, stroke, or death during a six-year period. Even when blood pressure, smoking, and age were taken into consideration, the association persisted.

Gum and mints are frequently sweetened with xylitol.

That risk remained 18% greater over the whole 30-year period. Dr. Marco Witkowski, the study's author, acknowledged that the results demonstrate "how little we know" about these additions over the long term and suggested a potential mechanism: xylitol may make blood stickier and thicker, increasing the chance of clots.

An internal investigation released late Thursday found former Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer allowed harassment of staffers, had an inappropriate relationship with a security aide and used government funds for personal travel.

posts.title: Jeju Police Officer Arrested After 298 Missing-Person Cases Come Under Scrutiny
posts.subheadline: A case involving two people later found dead has exposed a much wider problem, prompting authorities to review every missing-person report handled by the officer.
posts.bodyContent:
A missing-person case is supposed to trigger a search for answers. On South Korea's Jeju Island, authorities are now investigating how one police officer came to handle 298 missing-person reports, after allegations that he improperly closed cases without properly confirming that people were safe.

The officer, identified by his surname Bu, was arrested on August 25, 2026, on allegations including dereliction of duty, falsifying official electronic records and obstructing official duties. He has denied the allegations, although police said he later partially admitted to falsely telling the boyfriend of one missing woman that he had contacted her and confirmed she was safe.

The scandal began to unravel after two missing-person cases handled by Bu were found to have been closed prematurely. One involved 37-year-old Jang Mi-ran, who disappeared in May. Police later found a body believed to be hers on August 24, around 104 days after she went missing. Investigators found no call records supporting Bu's claim that he had spoken with her.

Another case involved a man in his 60s who had also been reported missing. His body was found after the case had allegedly been closed without proper confirmation of his safety.

posts.title: ‘By Any Means’ Review: Mark Wahlberg’s Gangster for a Good Cause
posts.subheadline: The actor stars alongside Yahya Abdul-Mateen II as a mob hitman enlisted by the FBI to help investigate a racist murder in 1960s Mississippi in this bare-knuckle historical drama.
posts.bodyContent:
“By Any Means” suggests it takes a dirty man to clean up a historically and culturally entrenched mess. We’re in 1966 Mississippi, where a straitlaced black FBI agent (Yahya Abdul-Mateen II) and a career criminal (Mark Wahlberg) become unlikely partners in an effort to solve a racist murder. Welcome to a race-swapped “48 Hrs.” with a heart of righteous fury.  

Civil-rights dramas tend to be preachy and self-congratulatory, painting halos on the white saviors and the black victims, but the rousing “By Any Means” takes a literally punchy approach. It filters the trauma of race-based suffering through a genre piece about busting heads. Setting out to rebut the sanctimony of, say, “To Kill a Mockingbird,” with its holy glow, the feature directed by Elegance Bratton (“The Inspection”) has more of a “Dirty Harry” vibe. In a system corrupted by racism, justice is sometimes unattainable. If they mess with you, notes Mr. Wahlberg’s character, you’re allowed to mess with them, except he uses a different verb than “mess.”

posts.title: ‘Frederick Douglass’s American Founding’ and ‘Until the Last Yoke Is Broken’: A Foundational Question
posts.subheadline: Frederick Douglass’s early speeches condemned the U.S. Constitution for embedding slavery in its clauses. Decades later, he saw the document very differently.
posts.cardSummary: Is the Constitution—the original one of 1787, before the later rights-extending amendments—pro-slavery or antislavery? The question was an urgent one to America...
posts.bodyContent:
Is the Constitution—the original one of 1787, before the later rights-extending amendments—pro-slavery or antislavery? The question was an urgent one to Americans amid the rising tensions leading up to the Civil War.

As a young abolitionist, Frederick Douglass (1818-95) denounced the Constitution as “nothing more than a compromise with man-stealers, and a cunningly devised complication of falsehoods, calculated to deceive foreign nations into a belief that this is a free country.” By the early 1850s, however, he had reversed himself. Properly interpreted, he declared, the Constitution was “a glorious liberty document.” That startling conversion is the subject of Dennis C. Rasmussen’s “Frederick Douglass’s American Founding,” an engaging, lucid intellectual history. Bradley N. Rebeiro’s “Until the Last Yoke Is Broken” asks the next question: What constitutional theory allowed Douglass to reach so unlikely a conclusion?

When Uganda enacted one of the world’s strictest antigay laws in 2023, the Biden administration imposed visa restrictions on its top officials and moved to cut off the country’s goods from U.S. markets. The Trump administration, in contrast, was silent last month when Ghana’s Parliament passed sweeping antigay legislation.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Congo’s Ebola Outbreak Reaches Territory Held by Islamic State
posts.subheadline: Militant violence creates no-go zone for health responders as virus spreads
posts.cardSummary: NAIROBI—A rare strain of Ebola has reached a corner of the Democratic Republic of Congo controlled by Islamic State militants, a place too dangerous for health ...
posts.bodyContent:
NAIROBI—A rare strain of Ebola has reached a corner of the Democratic Republic of Congo controlled by Islamic State militants, a place too dangerous for health workers fighting to stop the deadly virus.

The Bundibugyo strain has killed one person in the militant-controlled territory of Mambasa, which is some 100 miles from the outbreak’s epicenter in a gold-mining town of Mongbwalu. Mambasa is the stronghold of the Allied Democratic Forces, an Islamic State affiliate conducting an insurgency against Congolese and Ugandan troops.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Ebola Outbreak Is Now Third Largest in History. Here’s What to Know.
posts.subheadline: Vaccine developers are moving quickly as a rare Ebola strain spreads in a volatile region of Democratic Republic of Congo
posts.cardSummary: An outbreak of a rare strain of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo is already the third largest in history, just weeks after it likely began.It is spread...
posts.bodyContent:
An outbreak of a rare strain of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo is already the third largest in history, just weeks after it likely began.

It is spreading rapidly in one of the most volatile and vulnerable regions of the world, worrying U.S. and international health officials. Cuts to international health aid over the past year and a half are adding to the burden, some public-health leaders say.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Trump Wants Minerals, Health Data for Aid. African Nations Are Pushing Back.
posts.subheadline: Governments bridle at U.S. demands for private medical data and, in some cases, access to minerals
posts.cardSummary: A handful of African nations are rejecting American health aid, outraged by the Trump administration’s demands for access to private health records and even min...
posts.bodyContent:
A handful of African nations are rejecting American health aid, outraged by the Trump administration’s demands for access to private health records and even minerals in exchange for lifesaving medicine.

A year after President Trump reversed decades of American policy toward poor countries and closed the U.S. Agency for International Development, some African governments are bridling at the conditions he has set for resuming funding to combat AIDS, tuberculosis and malaria.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Court Blocks Trump Administration Plan to Treat American Ebola Patients in Kenya
posts.subheadline: Kenyan judge halts construction and operations of a tented U.S. field hospital
posts.cardSummary: NAIROBI—A Kenyan high court put a temporary hold on the Trump administration’s plan to set up an Ebola quarantine-and-treatment facility for Americans in the Ea...
posts.bodyContent:
NAIROBI—A Kenyan high court put a temporary hold on the Trump administration’s plan to set up an Ebola quarantine-and-treatment facility for Americans in the East African country.

Hours after the U.S. said it had sealed a deal with Kenya to erect a tented field hospital on a Kenyan air base, the court on Friday halted construction and barred medical operations while a lawsuit objecting to the plan is pending.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: U.S. Says Deal Reached With Kenya on Ebola Quarantine Facility for Americans
posts.subheadline: Agreement comes amid local outrage in Kenya
posts.cardSummary: The Trump administration said Thursday it had reached a deal with Kenya to establish a quarantine facility for Americans exposed to Ebola in the Democratic Repu...
posts.bodyContent:
The Trump administration said Thursday it had reached a deal with Kenya to establish a quarantine facility for Americans exposed to Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo, an arrangement that has drawn fierce opposition from Kenyan medical groups.

In a conference call with reporters, senior administration officials said more than 30 U.S. public-health officers were en route to staff the 50-bed unit, which will be located at the Laikipia Air Base outside the city of Nanyuki and operational beginning Friday. The deployed officers include physicians, nurses, therapists and technologists, one of the officials said, including those who have experience dealing with prior Ebola outbreaks.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: U.S. Races to Set Up Quarantine Facility in Kenya for Americans Exposed to Ebola
posts.subheadline: Move is a departure from procedure used during previous outbreaks of the virus
posts.cardSummary: WASHINGTON—The Trump administration is expected to deploy U.S. public-health officers to Kenya to staff a potential quarantine facility there amid the Ebola out...
posts.bodyContent:
WASHINGTON—The Trump administration is expected to deploy U.S. public-health officers to Kenya to staff a potential quarantine facility there amid the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to people familiar with the matter.

The people said the facility, which Tuesday was pending signoff from the Kenyan government, is primarily intended for Americans who are exposed to or at high risk of testing positive for the virus in the region, as well as Americans who test positive.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: China Eliminates Tariffs on Africa to Outmaneuver Trump
posts.subheadline: Beijing’s ‘politically astute’ move contrasts with U.S. tariff barrage
posts.cardSummary: JOHANNESBURG—African countries are finding it harder to export to the U.S. since President Trump returned to the White House with a long list of tariffs. But Ch...
posts.bodyContent:
JOHANNESBURG—African countries are finding it harder to export to the U.S. since President Trump returned to the White House with a long list of tariffs. But China sees their struggle as an opportunity.

Since May 1, Beijing has removed tariffs on all goods from 53 of 54 African nations in an effort to win business and influence across the continent. Everything from wine to sesame seeds and wool has been entering China tariff-free from everywhere except tiny Eswatini, which maintains diplomatic ties with Taiwan. Analysts say the move could push Africa’s population of more than a billion people and vast mineral resources further into China’s orbit.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Deep Distrust, Superstition Impede Efforts to Contain Ebola
posts.subheadline: Grieving families are fighting medical personnel for access to bodies as misinformation worsens the outbreak
posts.cardSummary: NAIROBI—When Red Cross volunteers cocooned in hazmat suits and face shields arrived at a small hospital in the Democratic Republic of Congo this weekend to disp...
posts.bodyContent:
NAIROBI—When Red Cross volunteers cocooned in hazmat suits and face shields arrived at a small hospital in the Democratic Republic of Congo this weekend to dispose of the remains of a popular local preacher, they found themselves in a fast-escalating confrontation with relatives who insisted on touching the highly infectious corpse.

The volunteers waved the man’s family members away from the Ebola isolation tent at Mongbwalu General Hospital, where his body lay on a plastic sheet on the floor.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Doctors, Hospitals Struggle to Keep Up With Ebola’s Spread
posts.subheadline: ‘Hospitals are fighting with no tools at all,’ says director-general of Africa’s CDC as fast-spreading Congo outbreak overwhelms resources
posts.cardSummary: NAIROBI, Kenya—The fast-spreading Ebola virus is overwhelming creaking hospitals and clinics in the Democratic Republic of Congo, dimming hopes for quick contai...
posts.bodyContent:
NAIROBI, Kenya—The fast-spreading Ebola virus is overwhelming creaking hospitals and clinics in the Democratic Republic of Congo, dimming hopes for quick containment of what is already the third-largest outbreak of the killer disease in history.

With at least 750 suspected cases and an official death count of 177 as of this weekend—the actual toll is likely higher—patients are being treated in ordinary wards because of a lack of dedicated Ebola treatment centers in the hardest-hit areas, according to the Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Vance’s 2028 Audition With Voters Has Begun
posts.subheadline: Plus, Sen. Fetterman is showing little interest in his job, and some Republicans worry about having Trump at the center of their midterms campaign
posts.cardSummary: Good morning. The past couple of weeks have shown the gauntlet Vice President JD Vance will have to navigate if he seeks to sew up the GOP nomination for presid...
posts.bodyContent:
Good morning. The past couple of weeks have shown the gauntlet Vice President JD Vance will have to navigate if he seeks to sew up the GOP nomination for president in 2028.

He will need to stay close to President Trump while also owning the fact that he is not President Trump.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Behind Closed Doors, John Fetterman Shows Little Interest in the Work of a Senator
posts.subheadline: Poised to be a possible swing vote in a divided Congress, he churns through staff as he dodges constituents, alienates fellow Democrats and courts Israel lobby
posts.cardSummary: One morning in June, three paralyzed military veterans in wheelchairs from rural Pennsylvania arrived at the office of Sen. John Fetterman for a long-awaited me...
posts.bodyContent:
One morning in June, three paralyzed military veterans in wheelchairs from rural Pennsylvania arrived at the office of Sen. John Fetterman for a long-awaited meeting to discuss legislation that would improve their care. 

Fetterman’s staff greeted them with bad news: The Pennsylvania Democrat had to cancel. He’d told his staff he may have eaten something bad and wasn’t feeling well, according to people familiar with the matter.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Missouri Supreme Court Rules State Can’t Use Redrawn Map in Midterms
posts.subheadline: Trump blasts the ruling, which is a blow to Republicans who were hoping to gain one House seat with new map
posts.cardSummary: The Missouri Supreme Court ruled Thursday that the state can’t use redrawn congressional districts that could have benefited Republicans in November’s midterm e...
posts.bodyContent:
The Missouri Supreme Court ruled Thursday that the state can’t use redrawn congressional districts that could have benefited Republicans in November’s midterm elections, and voters must decide if they should be used in future elections.

The unanimous decision was a blow to Republicans who were hoping to gain one U.S. House seat with the redrawn map in the midterms. Around the country, both parties have been changing congressional maps hoping to gain an advantage in the House.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Trump Names Adam Telle Acting Army Secretary After Driscoll Resignation
posts.subheadline: Telle is the current assistant secretary of the Army for civil works
posts.cardSummary: President Trump named Adam Telle as acting Army secretary, succeeding Dan Driscoll, who resigned earlier this week after months of tension with Defense Secretar...
posts.bodyContent:
President Trump named Adam Telle as acting Army secretary, succeeding Dan Driscoll, who resigned earlier this week after months of tension with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

Trump said Telle, assistant secretary of the Army for civil works, would start in his new job immediately. “He is a Great Patriot, who is respected by all,” Trump said Thursday evening on Truth Social.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Trump Administration Again Asks Supreme Court to Allow New Mail Voting Rules
posts.subheadline: Latest appeal seeks to clear the way for the Postal Service to enforce the rules ahead of November’s midterm elections
posts.cardSummary: WASHINGTON—The Trump administration’s bid to deploy the U.S. Postal Service to regulate mail-in ballots is back at the Supreme Court for the second time in as m...
posts.bodyContent:
WASHINGTON—The Trump administration’s bid to deploy the U.S. Postal Service to regulate mail-in ballots is back at the Supreme Court for the second time in as many weeks.

In an emergency appeal on Thursday, the administration asked the high court to allow it to immediately implement proposed rules that would require states to hand over voter data and would give the Postal Service power to reject mail ballots that don’t comply with new conditions.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Work on Trump’s 250-Foot Arch in Washington to Start in Next Two Weeks
posts.subheadline: Plan to build structure between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery faces legal challenges
posts.cardSummary: Excavation work on President Trump’s 250-foot-tall arch in Washington, is expected to start over the next two weeks, the administration said Thursday. The proje...
posts.bodyContent:
Excavation work on President Trump’s 250-foot-tall arch in Washington, is expected to start over the next two weeks, the administration said Thursday. 

The project, one of Trump’s many so-called beautification projects in the nation’s capital, is facing litigation. Opponents have argued Trump needs congressional approval to build it. The triumphal arch would block or disrupt the sightline of other monuments, critics have said.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Stocks Rally After Fed Official’s Comments on Holding Rates Steady
posts.subheadline: Plus, vibes from Trump and Vance, and the IRS looks to influence higher ed policies
posts.cardSummary: This is an edition of the What’s News newsletter, which helps you catch up on the headlines and understand the news, free in your inbox daily. If you’re not sub...
posts.bodyContent:
This is an edition of the What’s News newsletter, which helps you catch up on the headlines and understand the news, free in your inbox daily. If you’re not subscribed, sign up here.

1. Stocks climbed and global bond yields retreated.

The market moves followed comments by Fed governor Christopher Waller, who said he would support holding interest rates steady if August inflation data supports it. The odds of a Fed rate increase this month are now a coin flip, according to CME FedWatch, down from a 70% likelihood yesterday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.2%, the S&P 500 added 1.1%, and the Nasdaq composite climbed 1.4%.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Shock Defections Challenge Top Democrat Hakeem Jeffries
posts.subheadline: Two centrists side with Republicans on critical House vote, blindsiding the potential future speaker
posts.cardSummary: WASHINGTON—The surprise defections of two Democrats on a Republican procedural vote has sparked soul-searching in the party and raised new questions about wheth...
posts.bodyContent:
WASHINGTON—The surprise defections of two Democrats on a Republican procedural vote has sparked soul-searching in the party and raised new questions about whether Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries—the possible next House speaker—has the muscle to keep members in line. 

House Democrats were stunned when Reps. Jared Golden (D., Maine) and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (D., Wash.), two centrist members, voted this week to narrowly advance a rules package by a 210-208 tally. That allowed Republicans to then move forward on a series of votes, including a resolution condemning socialism that was designed to embarrass Democrats. Members of the minority party rarely help the majority party pass such rules.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Vance Defends Friendship With Trump Critic Tucker Carlson
posts.subheadline: Some Republicans have called on vice president to distance himself from former Fox News host
posts.cardSummary: WASHINGTON—Vice President JD Vance defended his friendship with former Fox News host Tucker Carlson, rejecting pressure from some Republicans to distance himsel...
posts.bodyContent:
WASHINGTON—Vice President JD Vance defended his friendship with former Fox News host Tucker Carlson, rejecting pressure from some Republicans to distance himself from the conservative iconoclast.

“Tucker is a friend, despite the fact that we disagree on a number of things,” Vance told reporters Thursday at the White House. “And I’m not going to play the game where I throw friends under the bus because I have political disagreements with them.”
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Leon Black Sues House Committee Over Epstein Probe
posts.subheadline: Billionaire won’t appear before House panel, claims it cannot compel him to turn over nondisclosure agreements with women
posts.cardSummary: Leon Black is suing the House Oversight Committee probing his ties with Jeffrey Epstein and refusing to turn over some nondisclosure agreements, arguing the pan...
posts.bodyContent:
Leon Black is suing the House Oversight Committee probing his ties with Jeffrey Epstein and refusing to turn over some nondisclosure agreements, arguing the panel and its chair have overstepped their authority.

Black, the co-founder of Apollo Global Management, was scheduled to appear Thursday before the Oversight Committee for a second round of questioning. He won’t appear. Instead, he filed a lawsuit in federal court against the committee and its Republican chair, Rep. James Comer (R., Ky.).
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Tillis Wants Hegseth Fired. Is the Pentagon Chief in Trouble?
posts.subheadline: Plus, the U.S.’s nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia includes a road map for enriching uranium, and the odd political alliance opposing data centers
posts.cardSummary: Good morning. The aftershocks of Army Secretary Dan Driscoll’s resignation this week continue to rumble.On Wednesday, Sen. Thom Tillis (R., N.C.) called for Pre...
posts.bodyContent:
Good morning. The aftershocks of Army Secretary Dan Driscoll’s resignation this week continue to rumble.

On Wednesday, Sen. Thom Tillis (R., N.C.) called for President Trump to replace Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The retiring senator’s critique of the Pentagon chief was harsh.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Hegseth Extends Mideast Deployments Into 2027, Escalating Strain on Troops
posts.subheadline: Trump has told aides privately that he believes his strategy will eventually work, as 50,000 troops remain on hand to give him options
posts.cardSummary: When the U.S. launched its campaign against Iran six months ago, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth promised a quick, decisive blow that would avoid a long entangle...
posts.bodyContent:
When the U.S. launched its campaign against Iran six months ago, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth promised a quick, decisive blow that would avoid a long entanglement. Now, he is quietly extending troop deployments in a sign that the conflict could drag well into next year, according to people familiar with the matter.

It is part of an open-ended military strategy designed to give President Trump options in the war, the people said. But the deployment of 19 warships, air-defense units, fighter squadrons and paratroopers across the region is straining servicemembers and their families and creating a maintenance backlog that could take years to unwind, the people said.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Ted Cruz Is Testing the Waters for a 2028 Run—and Taking Swipes at JD Vance
posts.subheadline: The Texas senator is making trips to Iowa, promoting his book and hitting the podcast circuit as he considers joining the race to succeed Trum
posts.cardSummary: CLIVE, Iowa—Ted Cruz isn’t hiding his presidential ambitions—and he is taking some digs at the presumptive front-runner along the way.The 2028 contest hasn’t st...
posts.bodyContent:
CLIVE, Iowa—Ted Cruz isn’t hiding his presidential ambitions—and he is taking some digs at the presumptive front-runner along the way.

The 2028 contest hasn’t started yet, and there is still a midterm election in November. Vice President JD Vance, who is leading in early polls of potential Republican nominees, is campaigning for candidates in tough races and fundraising for the party.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Sen. Ed Markey Trounces Younger Challenger in Massachusetts
posts.subheadline: The 80-year-old prevails in the Democratic primary over Rep. Seth Moulton
posts.cardSummary: WASHINGTON—Massachusetts Sen. Ed Markey, who has spent nearly half a century in Congress, easily beat back a Democratic primary challenge Tuesday from Rep. Seth...
posts.bodyContent:
WASHINGTON—Massachusetts Sen. Ed Markey, who has spent nearly half a century in Congress, easily beat back a Democratic primary challenge Tuesday from Rep. Seth Moulton in a generational fight that focused on Markey’s age and the future of the party.

Markey, an 80-year-old liberal who has focused on climate change, defeated Moulton, a 47-year-old congressman who has frequently tangled with establishment figures within the party.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Do Democrats Have a Hasan Piker Problem?
posts.subheadline: Plus, the Postal Service faces mail-ballot allegations, and the U.S. renews strikes on Iran
posts.cardSummary: Good morning. Hasan Piker, an online streamer and unapologetic provocateur, has emerged as a polarizing figure in this 2026 election cycle. He is forcing Democr...
posts.bodyContent:
Good morning. Hasan Piker, an online streamer and unapologetic provocateur, has emerged as a polarizing figure in this 2026 election cycle. He is forcing Democrats to wrestle with a very uncomfortable question: How fringe are they willing to become?

Piker has said controversial things that have been well-documented about Sept. 11 and American Jews, among other things. Many Democrats try to wave him away. But he’s not a nobody. He has campaigned with Abdul El-Sayed, a bit of a provocateur himself who also happens to be the Democrats’ candidate for Senate in Michigan. Piker was at El-Sayed’s primary election night party and even spoke to the cameras after El-Sayed won.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: What to Know About Mail-Ballot Allegations Against the Postal Service
posts.subheadline: An anonymous complaint and fast-moving litigation challenge Trump administration’s claims that it can implement rules without disruption
posts.cardSummary: A Democratic senator on Tuesday released whistleblower allegations that the U.S. Postal Service has botched its implementation of mail-in ballot restrictions, a...
posts.bodyContent:
A Democratic senator on Tuesday released whistleblower allegations that the U.S. Postal Service has botched its implementation of mail-in ballot restrictions, a move that comes as the Trump administration plays defense in court over the legality of the new regulations.

The litigation could be back in front of the Supreme Court in a matter of days or weeks, casting uncertainty over a method of voting used by one in three Americans that nevertheless has come in for sharp criticism by President Trump.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: An $88,600 Photo With Trump: GOP Hopes to Raise Millions During Convention
posts.subheadline: Republican National Committee plans pair of high-dollar fundraisers during this month’s midterm convention in Dallas
posts.cardSummary: WASHINGTON—Republicans are planning to raise millions of dollars during the coming GOP midterm convention in Dallas, including asking donors to pay more than $8...
posts.bodyContent:
WASHINGTON—Republicans are planning to raise millions of dollars during the coming GOP midterm convention in Dallas, including asking donors to pay more than $88,000 for a photo with President Trump.

The Republican National Committee sent out invitations this week to a pair of fundraising events during the convention. A roundtable with Trump on Sept. 9 will cost $250,000 a person to attend, according to the invitation, which was reviewed by The Wall Street Journal. Donors can also take a photo with the president for $88,600.
posts.author: Jane

posts.title: House Passes Measure Funding Government Past the Midterms
posts.subheadline: Republicans and Democrats are eager to avoid another shutdown drama as they focus on re-election
posts.bodyContent:
WASHINGTON—The House overwhelmingly passed a bipartisan resolution to fund the government past a Sept. 30 deadline, with both Democrats and Republicans eager to avoid a shutdown and leave Washington as soon as possible to campaign ahead of the midterms.

The resolution, which passed 370-48, extends current funding levels through Dec. 11. The Senate passed the stopgap spending bill last month, and it now goes to President Trump’s desk.
posts.author: Yapa

posts.title: A Nation’s Soccer Hero: The Superfan Who Says He Can Stop Goals
posts.subheadline: Congolese man’s motionless presence is seen as so critical to the team’s success that the president intervened to get him to the U.S.
posts.cardSummary: KAMPALA, Uganda—Michel Kuka Mboladinga is on a mission so critical that the president of the Democratic Republic of Congo personally intervened so he could carr...
posts.bodyContent:
KAMPALA, Uganda—Michel Kuka Mboladinga is on a mission so critical that the president of the Democratic Republic of Congo personally intervened so he could carry it out on his behalf. 

The task: stop the country’s World Cup opponents from scoring.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Pro-Business Leader Wins Re-Election in Zambia Vote Marred by Fraud Allegations
posts.subheadline: H.H., as supporters call him, plans to triple copper production by 2031
posts.bodyContent:
KAMPALA, Uganda— Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema, the pro-business leader of Africa’s No. 2 copper producer, won a second five-year term in a vote marred by opposition allegations of fraud and repression.

The 64-year-old economist and rancher, who entered the race widely expected to win, secured 61.4% of five million votes cast, well ahead of his closest rival, Brian Mundubile, who garnered 38%, the Electoral Commission of Zambia announced Tuesday. The wide margin of victory allowed Hichilema to avoid a runoff.
posts.author: Oshidi

posts.title: Kenya Helicopter Crash Leaves 7 Dead, Including 5 Americans
posts.subheadline: A Telemundo executive and an Ecuador intelligence chief are among the victims
posts.cardSummary: Seven people, including five Americans, were killed in a helicopter crash in Kenya Wednesday, according to the State Department and local officials.The aircraft...
posts.bodyContent:
Seven people, including five Americans, were killed in a helicopter crash in Kenya Wednesday, according to the State Department and local officials.

The aircraft went down in Samburu County, Kenya, about eight hours north of Nairobi, a State Department spokesperson said. Seven people were aboard the helicopter, which crashed around 9:13 a.m. local time, according to Kenya’s Civil Aviation Authority. Samburu County Police Commander David Nkoroi said all seven died at the scene.
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: U.S. Begins Deporting Immigrants to Liberia
posts.subheadline: The West African nation recently agreed with the Trump administration to accept up to 1,200 people in the next year
posts.cardSummary: The U.S. has begun deporting immigrants to Liberia, officials in the West African country said, part of President Trump’s wider plan to send migrants to third-p...
posts.author: Mayon

posts.title: Washington’s Deadly New Headache: an al Qaeda-Houthi Terrorist Alliance
posts.subheadline: One man helped broker an arms trade between two militant groups that threatens another key oil-shipping route in the Middle East
posts.bodyContent:
On a balmy evening, Jibril “One-Armed” Yahya Ali and his new bride set out for a honeymoon drive along the beach outside al-Ghaydah, Yemen. 

Jibril, a Somali, and his Yemeni wife had met through a mutual acquaintance, an arms dealer who helped Jibril buy military-grade weapons from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. Jibril would then smuggle the arms to al-Shabaab, an Islamist insurgent group fighting to overthrow the government in Somalia.
posts.author: Ishmitha

posts.title: The Thai Town Hosting the USS Abraham Lincoln After a Grueling Deployment
posts.subheadline: About 5,000 sailors flush with cash and looking for R&R will pour into the seaside resort
posts.bodyContent:
PATTAYA, Thailand—At the Hottuna Bar in this seaside town, owner Suchet Teewiang will open a second counter to serve up ice-cold beers. Other venues on Walking Street, the city’s main drag, are staging DJ nights or bringing in extra hands to welcome the expected crowds.

Some 5,000 American sailors will pour into Pattaya starting Wednesday, when the USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier and two other Navy ships make a five-day port call in eastern Thailand.
posts.author: Ishmitha
